items.title: North Miami Beach High School's Andre Hyppolite is a finalist for the 2026 Nat Moore Trophy
items.text:
The two-way North Miami Beach senior, who was overlooked early in his career, says winning the award would validate years of work.

With the winner of the Nat Moore Trophy set to be announced in a little over two weeks, North Miami Beach High School senior Andre Hyppolite has emerged as a finalist for the honor recognizing South Florida's top high school football player."South Florida football is fast, physical, and competitive. It's just a different level; as everybody goes against each other, it's competition everywhere you go," Hyppolite said. A four-star recruit committed to the University of Miami, Hyppolite took an unconventional path to becoming one of the region's premier prospects. Considered a late bloomer who waited years for his opportunity on the varsity stage, he burst onto the recruiting radar during his junior season.Now in his senior campaign, Hyppolite has cemented his status as a dynamic two-way playmaker for North Miami Beach, contributing on both sides of the ball as a dual-threat quarterback and standout safety.Hyppolite wants to prove doubters wrong: "That's my motivation to keep showing who I am" Competing in one of the nation's deepest high school football hotbeds, Hyppolite has used being overlooked earlier in his career as fuel to elevate his game."I've been overlooked my whole life. It's not even football-related, but everything else, I always felt like I was the last person in the line, so being in this position and having this opportunity to feel different, showcase my abilities, and show who I am as a person, so that's my motivation to keep showing who I am," Hyppolite said. For a player who spent years biding his time to break through, winning the Nat Moore Award would represent more than an individual trophy—serving as validation for years of persistence and hard work."It would mean a lot; we put a lot of time and effort. We put a lot of blood, sweat, and tears into this, so it'll feel good to be rewarded," Hyppolite said. The 2026 Nat Moore Trophy winner will be named Dec. 1 at 7 p.m. during CBS News Miami's presentation show. You can vote for your favorite here.
items.desc: The two-way North Miami Beach senior, who was overlooked early in his career, says winning the award would validate years of work.

items.title: VICE CITY NIGHT: Miami Heat bring GTA 6 to life for epic showdown against the Bucks
items.text:
The Heat are taking things beyond their signature colors and special uniforms, with plans to transform the entire game-night atmosphere.

With the Milwaukee Bucks coming to town, the Heat are preparing for a major crossover between basketball and gaming, teaming up with Rockstar Games for a Grand Theft Auto 6-inspired takeover on Wednesday.
The collaboration has been more than two years in the making, with Miami Heat SVP, Brand and Chief Growth Officer Jennifer Alvarez revealing that the idea sparked when the team spotted its arena in the GTA 6 trailer.
“I actually can’t believe we’re here because it’s been over two years for us to get to this point,” Alvarez said.
The Heat’s connection to Vice dates back to 2017, making the partnership a perfect match. But the organization is taking things beyond its signature colors and special uniforms, with plans to transform the entire game-night atmosphere.
“So when you walk in the building, you actually live in Leonida. You don’t live in Florida,” Alvarez said, teasing the immersive experience that begins outside the arena.
The excitement extends to the court, where Miami’s players will sport special uniforms created for the occasion.
“They love the uniforms,” Alvarez said. “They know about what this moment means. And they’re excited that they get to be a part of it.”
The timing is no coincidence. The game is scheduled for Wednesday at 7 p.m., with doors opening at 5 p.m., just hours before GTA 6's planned midnight launch, placing the Heat at the center of a major moment for the gaming industry.
For Rockstar Games, the release follows a 13-year wait since Grand Theft Auto V debuted in 2013. For the Heat, it’s a chance to showcase the franchise’s creativity on a global stage.
“It’s going to be something that no other NBA fan has ever attended,” Alvarez said.
Between the exclusive uniforms, Giannis Antetokounmpo facing his former team, immersive entertainment and a Rockstar Games collaboration, Vice City Night is bringing a whole new meaning to Miami’s Vice identity!
items.desc: The Heat are taking things beyond their signature colors and special uniforms, with plans to transform the entire game-night atmosphere.

items.title: How Jarrett Kingston Is Emerging as the Best Waiver Wire Pick-Up for the Dolphins As Another One Bites the Dust
items.text:
Hours after the much-publicized move to waive kicker Zane Gonzalez, the Miami Dolphins made another transaction Monday, that one involving edge defender Jamree Kromah.
And, like Gonzalez, Kromah was waived, ending his brief time in Miami that began after he was claimed off waivers from the Chicago Bears.
Kromah was let go after appearing in two games for Miami, including the 24-22 loss against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday when his playing time occurred strictly on special teams.
The move left the Dolphins with three openings on their 53-man roster because they were at 52 players when they faced the Colts and haven't yet replaced either Gonzalez or Kromah.
More significantly, the move with Kromah provided more evidence that picking up players on waivers is a sound practice for rebuilding teams looking for hidden gems wherever they can find them, but it also rarely provides great answers.
This isn't to suggest the Dolphins should stop looking at the waiver wire in the hope of finding a good player on whom another team gave up too quickly, but at the same time understanding that the pieces to what the organization ultimately hopes is a contender likely will come through other methods, such as the draft or free agency.
Kromah was the 16th and most recent waiver wire acquisition by the Dolphins so far in 2026, a total that's just four shy of what they did in 2019 when they were undergoing another rebuilding project.
Of those 16 players picked up through waivers this year, exactly half already have come and gone. Of the other eight, only safety Julius Wood and guard Jarrett Kingston have started a game, and it's been one start each.
At this time, none of the waiver wire pick-ups has a significant role, though Wood is a core special teams player and Kingston just became the team's sixth offensive lineman for the game against Indianapolis on Sunday.
But the chances of any of the waiver wire pick-ups becoming key contributors on the team's road back to contention are pretty slim, and that's just the reality of making those moves.
And the Dolphins likely aren't done with moves like that because, who knows, maybe one of them could turn into Zach Sieler.
That's what happened in 2019 when the Dolphins claimed the defensive lineman from the Baltimore Ravens. Nearly seven years later, Sieler is well established as a core player for the Dolphins, a team captain and a major loss now that he's on IR.
To a much lesser degree, the Dolphins also hit in 2019 with Mack Hollins, but the success stories are extremely rare when it comes to waiver wire pick-ups.
It's why we always caution against expecting too much whenever a newcomer arrives, whether it's Kromah or even former Seattle Seahawks third-round pick Christian Haynes, who was claimed just a few days before Kromah.
The rationale is pretty simple: There's a reason the player's former team let them go.
Yes, there will be an exception to the rule at some point, which is why there's no harm in "turning over stones," as the saying goes. That's what the Dolphins did with Kromah.
And even though it didn't pan out, it still was worth the gamble.

October 28 — G Christian Haynes from Seattle ... No games played yet
October 13 — WR Jared Wayne from Houston ... Two games played
October 9 — RB Kaytron Allen from Washington ... Four games played

items.title: Man arrested after stealing $200K worth of cars from Hialeah Gardens dealership, police say
items.text:
HIALEAH GARDENS, FLA. (WSVN) - Police arrested a man after saying he stole several pricey rides from a car dealership in Hialeah Gardens.
Thirty-five-year-old Michael Guevara appeared in bond court on Monday, where he faces several charges.
“You were arrested for burglary. Five counts of grand theft from a vehicle, possession of burglary tools,” said Judge Mindy S. Glazer.
According to police, Guevara committed a hefty heist at Cabrera’s Auto on Sunday.
Surveillance video captures him scouting the area in the early morning hours. Then he heads to the back of the establishment, where he picks up a crowbar and claw hammer, then makes his way to the front and breaks into the store.
“He destroyed a bunch of things,” said dealership owner Ramon Cabrera.
Cabrera realized his dealership had been targeted and raced over to find a mess and several pricey rides missing.
“I hurried over here and noticed that the bar was pried open and the five cars were missing,” he said.
Cameras captured Guevara rummaging through bags, spraying Cabrera’s cologne and even changing his outfit.
“He actually ate a lot of candy, and later the wrappers were found inside the BMW, and he sprayed on some of my cologne! Wow, he was in the middle of a five-vehicle theft. I did find that a bit strange,” said Cabrera.
Guevara ultimately obtained the cars’ key fobs and began moving them away from the dealership.
“A 2019 Porsche Macan,” Cabrera said, describing one of the stolen cars.
The ambitious overnight car caper stole over $200,000 worth of vehicles, Cabrera said.
Investigators said Guevara dropped off the cars in various spots and took the BMW home. Police located the car parked at Guevara’s home using its tracking system.
The BMW still had its “For Sale” decal on its windshield when they encountered it.
When police saw Guevara approach the car outside the home, they ordered him to drop to the ground at gunpoint and made their arrest.
“Would your honor consider house arrest?” asked the public defender.
As for Cabrera’s Auto, the owner said police recovered the five vehicles undamaged, and they have since put bars back on the windows for protection.

items.title: Vehicle slams into daycare in northwest Miami-Dade during crash injuring 3 people, officials say
items.text:
The incident occurred in the area of NW 46th Street and 22nd Avenue, where It's a Small World Learning Center is located.

An investigation is underway in northwest Miami-Dade after first responders said three people were injured in a crash that sent a vehicle slamming into the side of a daycare on Monday afternoon.
Miami-Dade Fire Rescue told CBS News Miami that the incident occurred at approximately 12:48 p.m. in the area of NW 46th Street and 22nd Avenue, where It's a Small World Learning Center is located.
According to the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office, preliminary information indicates that the at-fault driver was traveling eastbound on NW 46th Street and, when the vehicle approached NW 22nd Avenue, failed to stop at the red traffic light. The driver collided with two other vehicles, and one of the vehicles, a silver Dodge Grand Caravan, was redirected toward the nearby learning center building as a result of the crash.
The Grand Caravan struck the structure, causing property damage.
Miami-Dade Fire Rescue said three people were injured, with the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office confirming the three as an adult female driver, an adult male driver, and a juvenile male who was attending the learning center for elementary and middle school students.
All three, according to MDSO, were taken to the hospital in stable condition.
No additional information was released, including whether the at-fault driver was injured or is facing any charges.
Representatives for It's a Small World Learning Center told CBS News Miami that they are not commenting about the crash.
items.desc: The incident occurred in the area of NW 46th Street and 22nd Avenue, where It's a Small World Learning Center is located.

items.title: Alex Rizo kicks off SD 39 campaign with more law enforcement endorsements
items.text:
‘I’m running for the Senate to continue delivering results, protecting our conservative values and ensuring our communities have a strong voice in Tallahassee.’

State Rep. Alex Rizo kicked off his Special Election campaign for Senate District 39 in his hometown of Hialeah with two more endorsements from law enforcement groups.
He picked up nods from the National Association of Police Organizations and the Florida Police Benevolent Association , the state’s largest law enforcement union.
They join three other public safety groups — Florida Professional Firefighters , the Florida State Fraternal Order of Police and the South Florida Police Benevolent Association — that are also backing Rizo’s effort to succeed fellow Republican and Lt. Gov.-elect Bryan Ávila .
He also carries support from U.S. Reps. Mario Díaz-Balart and Carlos Giménez , Gov. Ron DeSantis , Attorney General James Uthmeier , CFO Blaise Ingoglia , Senate President-designate Jim Boyd , state Sen. Jay Trumbull , all five of Miami-Dade County’s constitutional officers and a passel of local leaders and current and former elected officials.
“I’m incredibly grateful for the confidence and support of so many leaders who share my commitment to this community and the future of Florida,” Rizo said Thursday.
“This district is my home. It’s where I’ve raised my family, built relationships and had the privilege of serving our neighbors. From our small businesses and hardworking families to the law enforcement officers, firefighters and first responders who keep our communities safe, I know what makes this part of Miami-Dade special. I’m running for the Senate to continue delivering results, protecting our conservative values and ensuring our communities have a strong voice in Tallahassee.”
Rizo, a teacher and school administrator-turned-education consultant, chaired the Miami-Dade Republican Party from 2022 to 2024, when President Donald Trump became the first Republican presidential nominee since 1988 to carry the county .
Republicans that year also won every constitutional office race, and no seats in Congress or the Legislature changed hands.
Rizo entered the SD 39 race in early September, one day after fellow Hialeah Republican state Rep. David Borrero announced his bid.
Both were first elected to the House in 2020 and won re-election unopposed in June. Rizo represents House District 112, and Borrero represents House District 111. Both districts overlap with SD 39.
Ávila resigned his SD 39 seat in August to join Gov.-elect Byron Donalds’ ticket as his running mate.
SD 39 includes all or parts of Doral, Hialeah, Hialeah Gardens, Medley, Miami Lakes, Miami Springs, Sweetwater and Virginia Gardens. Republicans outnumber Democrats there by more than 2-to-1 .
items.desc: ‘I’m running for the Senate to continue delivering results, protecting our conservative values and ensuring our communities have a strong voice in Tallahassee.’
